en.title: EU Housing Simplification Feedback Sought to Improve Disability Accessibility
en.summary: The European Disability Forum invites feedback on its draft response to the EU Housing Simplification Package, aiming to shape accessibility‑focused housing policy. Meanwhile, a Route Fifty report finds most U.S. states compliant with federal website accessibility rules, and SEPTA has begun construction on a $44 million accessibility upgrade at Philadelphia’s 11th Street Station. Additional coverage includes a critique of inspiration porn, an examination of steep wheelchair ramps, and a discussion of the Möbius strip as a disability metaphor.

highlights.title: Call for feedback: EDF’s draft response to the call for evidence on the Housing Simplification Package
States are mostly compliant with website accessibility rule, report finds - Route Fifty
SEPTA breaks ground on 11th Street station accessibility improvements
Möbius Strip and Disability: Metaphor, Meaning, Uses

zh-TW.title: 歐洲殘疾論壇徵求住房簡化套件回應 以提升無障礙政策
zh-TW.summary: 歐洲殘疾論壇邀請利益相關者對其關於歐盟住房簡化套件證據徵求的草案回應提供意見，以影響有利於殘疾人士的住房政策。同時，報告顯示美國多數州已達成聯邦網站無障礙法規的合規，SEPTA 已在第11街車站啟動4400萬美元的無障礙改善工程。此外，日本厚生勞動省將規範殘障就業服務業，日本UNESCO 提供社區支援與資源，以促進殘障人士的社會參與。
